title: Satisfaction by a surety is imputed to the debtor
source_text: XIII. Porro Christi passionem, & obedientiam illam Deo Patri pro nobis praestitam usque ad mortem crucis nobis a Deo imputari, donari & communicari ii soli negare possunt, qui Christum morte sua pro peccatis nostris Deo satisfecisse negant. Neque enim percipi potest quomodo exhibita a vade satisfactio non imputetur ei cujus nomine facta est: Aut quomodo censeatur fidejussor aliquis creditor pecuniam pro debitore solvisse, & solutionem istam acceptasse creditor, & tamen solutam pecuniam non imputari debitori illi pro quo soluta est. Proinde quicunque fatetur Christum pro fidelibus morte sua satisfecisse, & poenas illis debitas dependisse, per evidentem & necessariam consequentiam agnoscit meritum mortis Christi & obedientiam ejus fidelibus a Deo donari atque imputari.
pass_a_gloss: Further, that Christ’s passion and that obedience rendered to God the Father for us unto the death of the cross are imputed, given, and communicated to us by God—only those can deny who deny that Christ by his death satisfied God for our sins. For it cannot be grasped how a satisfaction offered by a surety is not imputed to the one in whose name it was made; or how some surety is reckoned to have paid money to a creditor for a debtor, and the creditor to have accepted that payment, and yet the paid money not be imputed to that debtor for whom it was paid. Therefore whoever confesses that Christ by his death satisfied for the faithful and paid the penalties due to them, by evident and necessary consequence acknowledges that the merit of Christ’s death and his obedience are given and imputed by God to the faithful.
pass_b_english: Deny imputation only if you deny Christ’s death satisfied for our sins.
A surety’s accepted payment is imputed to the debtor in whose name it was made.
